US9884981013.note: Yum Brands Inc (NYSE: YUM), Louisville, Kentucky. AFSC: https://investigate.info/company/yum-brands — prisons flag only; zero Israel mentions; page valid as of 8 February 2024. Over 55,000 KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and The Habit Burger Grill restaurants in more than 155 countries; ~36,000 employees and $6.8bn revenue in 2022. Direct employment, not a supplier hole — same shape as Tyson and Wendy's, which is why it clears the Target/Kroger bar (those explicitly forbid prison labour in their supply chains). According to a class action filed December 2023, incarcerated individuals held in minimum-security prisons in Alabama are 'leased' out and transported to day jobs at fast-food chains including KFC, Burger King, McDonald's and Wendy's; under the convict-leasing system they are allegedly forced to work for wages lower than required by law, with long and demanding hours, sometimes unsafe conditions, and no ability to refuse or raise concerns without risking return to 'more violent and life-threatening' prisons. Policy gap recorded: Yum prohibits the use of forced labour but does not bar the use of all forms of prison labour. Evidentiary level noted honestly: an allegation in a filed complaint, not an adjudicated finding — the same level accepted for Tyson and Wendy's. Attribution noted: AFSC places the conduct on the KFC subsidiary rather than Yum itself, so the row sits on the parent's domain for a subsidiary's exposure. Existing PizzaHut rows on pizzahut.com (reason BDS_GRASS) already cover that brand separately. Reason c: US HQ.
